headline.headline: METS BATS STAY HOT ON ROAD AS BATY, ALVAREZ HOMER IN 4-1 WIN OVER PHILLIES
headline.deck: New York breaks open a pitchers' duel with a two-run seventh, silencing Citizens Bank Park
headline.body:
PHILADELPHIA — The New York Mets arrived at Citizens Bank Park on Thursday night and left with a 4-1 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies, powered by home runs from Brett Baty and Francisco Alvarez and a two-run seventh inning that broke open what had been a tense, scoreless affair.

For six innings, both sides traded zeroes before Baty delivered his fifth homer of the season in the third to stake the Mets to a 1-0 lead. The Phillies, in front of 40,109 fans, could not answer. Then in the seventh, the Mets doubled their advantage with a two-run frame that effectively sealed the result. Alvarez, who launched his 11th home run of the year, has emerged as one of the more dangerous power threats in the National League East. Philadelphia got on the board in the eighth on a Trea Turner solo shot, his 11th of the season, but the rally stalled there. The Mets added an insurance run in the ninth to make it 4-1 final.

Doubles from Ewing and Schwarber added to the offensive production, while Harper also went for two bases for Philadelphia in a losing effort. The Mets stranded 16 runners on base but managed to do the damage that mattered, outlasting the Phillies in 2 hours and 37 minutes. New York's win puts additional pressure on Philadelphia in the NL East standings entering the weekend.

secondary.headline: BLUES COMMIT $40.5 MILLION TO McMAICHAEL IN BOLD SECOND-ROUND MOVE
secondary.deck: St. Louis locks up recently acquired forward Connor McMichael as playoff run deepens
secondary.body:
ST. LOUIS — The Blues wasted no time turning a trade acquisition into a long-term investment. St. Louis announced Thursday that forward Connor McMichael has signed a six-year, $40.5 million contract extension, a deal averaging $6.75 million annually that signals the organization's confidence in the 24-year-old as a cornerstone piece.

The signing comes with the Blues still alive in the NHL playoff second round, a move that doubles as both a commitment to the present and a statement about the future. McMichael, acquired in a trade earlier this postseason, gives St. Louis a skilled, two-way center capable of contributing in all situations. At $6.75 million per year, the Blues are betting McMichael grows into that number through the prime years of his career.

secondary.headline: BLAZERS, RAPTORS AND GRIZZLIES PUSH DEEPER INTO SECOND ROUND WITH THURSDAY WINS
secondary.deck: Three playoff games delivered pivotal results as the conference semifinals heat up
secondary.body:
The NBA conference semifinals continued Thursday night with three games that tightened the picture across both brackets. Portland, Toronto and Memphis each recorded victories, keeping their respective series alive or extending leads as the playoff field narrows toward the conference finals.

The Blazers topped the Nuggets, the Raptors edged the Heat and the Grizzlies handled the Hawks in a crowded night of second-round action. With the playoffs moving deeper into May, each game now carries the weight of potential elimination pressure. The road to the NBA Finals is becoming clearer, and Thursday's results will reshape the outlook heading into the weekend slate.

secondary.headline: CUBS HOST TWINS TO OPEN THREE-GAME SET AS PITTSBURGH LOOKS TO EXTEND STREAK
secondary.deck: Chicago brings a four-game edge over .500 into a key interleague matchup at Wrigley Field
secondary.body:
CHICAGO — The Chicago Cubs, sitting at 54-42 and second in the NL Central, open a three-game series Friday against the Minnesota Twins, who come in at 48-49 and sitting third in the AL Central. The Cubs have played well enough this season to position themselves as a legitimate contender, and a strong showing against a Twins club hovering around .500 could help separate Chicago from the pack in its division.

Meanwhile, the Pittsburgh Pirates bring a winning streak into Cleveland for a Friday matchup against the Guardians. The Pirates are 50-47 and the Guardians 51-46, making this a genuine battle between two clubs fighting to stay relevant in the AL and NL Central races respectively. Also on the Friday schedule, the slumping Athletics, losers in their recent stretch at 41-55, visit the Washington Nationals in a game that offers both clubs a chance to salvage something before the All-Star break approaches.

column.headline: THE NHL'S 84-GAME SCHEDULE IS A CASH GRAB DRESSED UP AS PROGRESS
column.body:
The NHL announced Thursday that it is expanding the regular season from 82 to 84 games beginning in 2026-27, and the league would like you to believe this is about giving fans more hockey. It is not. It is about giving owners two more home dates and the television partners two more windows to sell advertising. The players, who already grind through one of the most physically punishing schedules in professional sports, will bear the cost of that arithmetic in sore joints and shortened careers.

The Blues signing Connor McMichael to a six-year deal worth $40.5 million in the middle of a playoff run is the kind of aggressive organizational thinking that wins championships. But adding games to a calendar that already asks too much of the human body is not aggressive thinking. It is greed wearing the jersey of ambition. The best thing the NHL could do for the long-term health of its product is protect the players who make it worth watching. Two extra games will not do that.

story.headline: METS SILENCE PHILLIES AT CITIZENS BANK, 4-1, AS BATY AND ALVAREZ GO DEEP
story.deck: New York's two-inning burst powers road win in NL East battle.
story.body:
PHILADELPHIA — The New York Mets needed just two big innings to walk out of Citizens Bank Park with a 4-1 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies on Thursday night, getting home runs from Brett Baty and Francisco Alvarez while holding the Phillies to a single run before 40,109 fans in a tidy two-hour, 37-minute affair.

Baty connected for his fifth home run of the season in the third inning to break a scoreless tie, and the Mets doubled down in the seventh, plating two more runs on a stretch that included Alvarez's 11th blast of the year. Trea Turner also went deep, accounting for his 11th homer, while Philadelphia managed only a Kyle Schwarber double and a Bryce Harper double among its few bright spots. The Phillies finally cracked the scoreboard in the eighth but could not generate any further damage against the Mets bullpen.

The Mets left 16 runners on base but did enough damage at the right moments to improve their standing in a tight NL East race. Philadelphia's offense, limited to seven stranded runners, never threatened seriously after the seventh-inning blow. The win sets up the final games of the series with New York holding the upper hand heading into the weekend.

story.headline: BLAZERS, RAPTORS, GRIZZLIES, WARRIORS, LAKERS ALL ADVANCE IN WILD THURSDAY PLAYOFF ACTION
story.deck: Five franchises punch tickets deeper into the bracket in an unforgettable night of basketball.
story.body:
The NBA playoffs delivered wall-to-wall drama Thursday as five games produced highlight-reel moments from coast to coast. The Portland Trail Blazers took down the Denver Nuggets in a hard-fought battle at Ball Arena, silencing a raucous Colorado crowd and pushing further into the bracket. Meanwhile, the Toronto Raptors outlasted the Miami Heat in a gritty contest that showcased why the Eastern Conference has been the most competitive bracket of the postseason.

Down in Memphis, the Grizzlies leaned on their suffocating defense to dispatch the Atlanta Hawks, keeping Ja Morant and company alive and dangerous heading into the next round. Out west, the Golden State Warriors reminded the basketball world that their championship pedigree never fades, dismantling the New York Knicks in what amounted to a clinic in ball movement and perimeter shooting at Chase Center.

The headline result of the night came out of Crypto.com Arena, where the Los Angeles Lakers finished off the Chicago Bulls to advance and set up what promises to be a blockbuster matchup in the next round. The Lakers rode a dominant interior presence and timely shot-making to put the Bulls away, sending the Staples faithful into a frenzy and reigniting championship talk in Hollywood heading into the weekend.

story.headline: BLUES LOCK UP McMAICHEL TO SIX-YEAR DEAL AS FLYERS MAKE ZEGRAS HIGHEST-PAID PLAYER
story.deck: St. Louis secures the former Capital while Philadelphia rewards its young pivot.
story.body:
ST. LOUIS — The Blues wasted no time cementing their offseason acquisition, signing forward Connor McMichael to a six-year, $40.5 million contract Friday, locking up the former Washington Capital at a $6.75 million annual average value. McMichael, 24, was acquired in a trade earlier this offseason and gives St. Louis a skilled, two-way center to anchor their middle-six for the better part of the decade. General manager Doug Armstrong has shown an aggressive hand this summer, and the McMichael signing signals the Blues believe they are building toward a serious contender in the Western Conference.

In Philadelphia, the Flyers moved decisively to retain one of the most electric offensive talents in the Eastern Conference, re-signing Trevor Zegras to a four-year deal worth $9.125 million per season. The contract makes Zegras the highest-paid player in franchise history, a significant commitment from an organization that has spent recent seasons rebuilding around younger talent. The 24-year-old winger dazzled opponents last season with his no-look passes and creative zone entries, giving Philadelphia a genuine star to market heading into the expanded 2026-27 campaign.

The backdrop for both signings is a league preparing for its largest scheduling shift in years. The NHL on Thursday released its 2026-27 regular-season schedule, confirming an expansion from 82 to 84 games, giving teams additional inventory for revenue and players additional opportunities to pile up statistics. The added games arrive as rosters across the league grow deeper and more competitive, and with McMichael now in St. Louis and Zegras locked into Philadelphia, two franchises enter the new era with their respective building blocks firmly in place.

story.headline: DRAFT GRADES ARE IN: EXPERTS SPLIT ON WHETHER TEAMS MADE RIGHT CALLS IN APRIL
story.deck: Analysts weigh in on which franchises won and lost the 2026 NFL Draft.
story.body:
The dust has settled on the 2026 NFL Draft, and the second-guessing is already in full swing. The Cleveland Browns, picking second overall, drew widespread praise for selecting USC quarterback Malik Jasper, a dual-threat talent who many scouts compared to a young Lamar Jackson. The Tennessee Titans, meanwhile, raised eyebrows by trading up four spots to grab a wide receiver in the first round despite glaring holes along their offensive line, a move that drew sharp criticism from analysts at NFL Network and Pro Football Focus alike.

Free agency drama continues to simmer well into May. Veteran pass rusher Micah Parsons, who hit the open market after the Dallas Cowboys declined to extend his contract last winter, finally agreed to a four-year, $112 million deal with the Los Angeles Rams, reuniting him with defensive coordinator Chris Shula. The signing gives the Rams what they believe is a legitimate edge threat opposite Kobie Turner and signals the franchise's intent to compete immediately despite questions at quarterback.

Training camp is still roughly two months away, but storylines are already building. In New England, rookie head coach Marcus Webb faces pressure to install an identity after the Patriots finished 6-11 in the 2025 season. In San Francisco, the 49ers are monitoring the recovery of running back Christian McCaffrey, who missed eight games last year with a hamstring injury. League observers say the next several weeks of roster moves will define which contenders are truly serious about challenging the defending Super Bowl LX champion Kansas City Chiefs.
